rationale: Contact time equation is physics, not biology. The constants in it (k_cat_eff, K_m_eff) depend on items 01-04 and are PLACEHOLDERS until those items are frozen.

where.tau: contact time (seconds) — time CSF spends in contact with enzyme membrane

frozen_equation.rationale: Contact time must be long enough for enzyme-substrate binding and catalysis, but short enough to maintain drainage (Q >= 0.05 mL/min).

where.f: fraction of Aβ cleared per pass through reactor
where.k_cat_eff: effective catalytic rate constant (s^-1) — BLOCKED on item 03
where.E_surf: enzyme surface density (mol/m^2) — BLOCKED on items 02, 03
where.K_m_eff: effective Michaelis constant (M) — BLOCKED on item 03
where.[S]: substrate concentration (M) — FROZEN at 0.1-0.2 nM from literature

clearance_model.rationale: 20% clearance per pass means with recirculation (CSF turns over ~3x/day), daily clearance ~60%. Significant but not total.

pulsation_synchronization_optimization.hypothesis: If tau is locked to the LOW-FLOW phase of pulsation (diastole), contact time is effectively longer without reducing total drainage.
pulsation_synchronization_optimization.model: tau_eff = tau_diastole = (1 + alpha) * tau_mean, where alpha is pulsation amplitude fraction (0.3-0.5)
pulsation_synchronization_optimization.predicted_clearance_enhancement: 1.3-1.5x compared to non-synchronized flow at same mean Q

what_is_frozen: The EQUATION FORM (tau = V/Q; f = 1 - exp(...)). The STRUCTURE of the model.
what_is_NOT_frozen: The constants k_cat_eff, E_surf, K_m_eff. These are placeholders (set to literature values for NEP, may not match our immobilized system).
what_unfreezes_constants: Resolution of items 01-04. Once we know which enzyme, which immobilization, measured kinetics, and CSF stability, we substitute real constants into the frozen equation.
constitutional_basis: Article XXVIII — the equation form is design work (frozen). The constants are measurement work (blocked). Distinguishing them prevents silent semantic promotion of literature constants into design constants.
